subject: Demo recap & proposed POC plan for Insurely
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellison <tom.ellison@insurely.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@insurely.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Demo recap + proposed POC plan (next steps)

Hi Tom / Priya 

Thanks again for taking the time today  appreciate you walking through the Insurely claims flow and the areas you want to speed up with an LLM-powered assistant. Quick recap from our demo and a proposed POC approach so we can align on success criteria and timing.

What we covered on the call
- Demo: Redwood chat endpoint integrated with a masked claims dataset (redacted PII)
- Key capabilities: structured extraction, guided question flows, and rerank for probable policy matches
- High-level architecture: customer data stays in your VPC during Private deployment; sandbox connectors for S3/DB access during the POC

Proposed 3-week POC (goal: evaluate latency, accuracy of extraction, and developer integration effort)
Week 0 (prep, 3-5 business days)
- Kickoff & mutual action plan (roles, Slack channel)
- Narrow evaluation set: 200 representative claims (sample provided by Insurely)
- Access: temporary service account + IP allowlist

Week 1 (integration + baseline)
- Redwood engineer paired session with your infra owner (Dylan suggested)
- Integrate the sandbox connector, ingest sample docs, baseline metrics collection (latency, tokens, error rate)
- Deliverable: demo of ingestion + baseline report

Week 2 (tuning + validation)
- Prompt engineering, schema tuning, and rerank thresholds
- Joint review of 50 flagged cases and scoring vs your current baseline

Week 3 (final evaluation & next steps)
- Final metrics report and knowledge transfer
- Decision gate: move to Dedicated or Private deployment, or extend POC for edge cases

Proposed success criteria (please validate)
- Latency: median response < 400ms for single-turn extraction on our Dedicated profile
- Accuracy: structured extraction F1 >= 0.85 on the evaluation set
- Integration effort: partner engineer can implement production call in <2 weeks after POC
- Security: no PII leaves your VPC during Private trial mode (well provide evidence via audit logs)

Attachments: Ieve attached a one-page POC outline (Insurely-POC-outline.pdf) and a draft SLA for review (SLA_Draft_v1.docx).

Next steps / asks for Insurely
1) Confirm the evaluation dataset (200 sample claims) and who will own delivery
2) Confirm technical contacts and preferred kickoff dates (we suggested Feb 24-26)
3) Confirm the success criteria above or send edits

If that looks good, Ill schedule the kickoff and loop in Dylan for the integration sessions and Alex for pricing/commit questions.

Thanks  excited to get started.


Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0187

[Attachment: Insurely-POC-outline.pdf (1 page, PDF)]

From: Tom Ellison <tom.ellison@insurely.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@insurely.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed POC plan (next steps)

Marissa 

Thanks for the clear recap and the POC outline  this is very helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side before we lock dates: 

1) Dataset: We can provide the 200 sample claims; Priya will own collecting and redacting PII. Can you confirm the format you prefer (JSONL with extracted fields vs. raw PDFs)?
2) Latency target: median <400ms seems aggressive  most of our users are okay with up to 500ms for extraction flows. Is 500ms achievable on Dedicated with the sample sizes we discussed?
3) Security: Good to hear about audit logs. Can you share the exact logs/fields well see during the Private trial? Well need that for our compliance review team.

Also, can you give a rough estimate of the engineer time Dylan will need during Week 1? We want to block calendar resources appropriately (we have limited bandwidth Feb 24-26).

If we can get these answered, we can confirm kickoff for Feb 25.

Best,
Tom
Head of Product | Insurely
Tom.Ellison@insurely.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellison <tom.ellison@insurely.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@insurely.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed POC plan (next steps)

Thanks Tom  great questions. Quick answers below and then a suggested revised plan given your bandwidth note.

Dataset format
- JSONL with one record per claim is ideal (fields: claim_id, incident_text, attachments_meta). We can accept raw PDFs too but JSONL speeds up automated evaluation.

Latency target
- 500ms median is reasonable. Our Dedicated profile for the POC should hit ~350-450ms depending on sequence length; well run the baseline tests in Week 1 and report. Ieve updated the success criteria to median <500ms to align with your expectation.

Security / audit logs
- During Private trial we provide request-level logs including timestamp, request_id, model_variant, latency_ms, auth_principal (service account), and an audit summary showing data ingress/egress. Well provide an export example ahead of kickoff.

Engineer time for Week 1
- Expect a 4-6 hour paired session (setup + smoke tests) and then ~2-3 hours asynchronously for follow-ups. If Feb 25 is the kickoff, well schedule the paired session on Feb 26 (US PT morning) to accommodate your team.

Revised timeline suggestion
- Kickoff: Feb 25  mutual action plan and dataset handoff
- Paired integration: Feb 26 (4-6 hour block)
- Baseline delivery: Feb 27
- Tuning & review: Mar 2-4
- Final report: Mar 6

Next steps
1) Priya -> share dataset by Feb 25 EOD (JSONL preferred)
2) Well schedule the Feb 26 integration block with Dylan
3) Alex will follow up on pricing/commit details after the baseline report

Ill attach an updated POC outline with the latency target changed to 500ms and an example audit log export for your compliance reviewers.


Marissa

[Attachment: Insurely-POC-outline.pdf (updated), SLA_Draft_v1.docx, example_audit_log.csv]

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>

Thanks everyone  looping in the infra playbook and a short checklist so Tom / Priya know what Ill need for the paired session.

Checklist (paired integration)
- Service account with S3 read access for the sample bucket or a link to the JSONL file
- IP allowlist + temp SSH bastion details if you want the connector to run inside your VPC
- Example claim (1-3 files) with expected extracted fields
- Contact for your network/security team (for quick firewall exceptions)

Estimate of effort
- Paired session (4-6 hours) to instrument the connector, run ingestion, and validate baseline metrics
- Follow-ups (2-4 hours) for tuning and log delivery

Tom/Priya  if Feb 26 works, Ill send a calendar invite with the session agenda and a Zoom link. Ill also drop a lightweight runbook to the shared Drive folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/insurely-poc).

Looking forward to it.
